translated_text: 3. .7.40 My darling, Unfortunately, I haven't received any letters from you since I left Périgueux. I don't know if you're still in Ligninac. Nevertheless, I hope you'll receive one from me from time to time. I'm still in Villeneuve and waiting for demobilization, but it could take some time. If possible, could you send me a telegram or a letter to Villeneuve Poste Restante? Perhaps I'll stay here a few more days. We don't know anything. There's nothing to do here—only wait, and it's terrible. In any case, I'll remain free for a while and I won't leave France. I hope everything will be alright and I'll be at your place soon. I just need to know where you are. I also want to look for my belongings because I still hope to find them. Unfortunately, I could only save my life like this. Personally, we're doing very well. I'm thinking a lot about what you'll do now, where you are, in good health – if you're well, if you're still with the family. It's terrible, nothing to know, and despite everything, we must remain calm and wise so as not to do anything foolish. I believe that up until now I've done everything right, and I hope I will continue to do so until we meet again. I adore you, my little wife, and I am always faithful to you. Your Bob. 4 7:40 JUL 40 Le Castel GARY LIGNON, Owner Consumption of 1 Brands Meeting of Mr. M. the Travelers Telephone 8 RC 612 Jugglest Villeneuve-sur-Lot FNEUVE 4 1540 JUIC 40 YONN Mrs. E.
